When the Sun, Moon, and Earth align during full and new moons, their gravitational forces combine to produce spring tides, which are especially high and low. Conversely, when the Sun and Moon form a right angle relative to Earth during quarter moons, their forces partially cancel, creating neap tides with less extreme ranges. Local geography significantly modifies these basic patterns.
